sentences.text: Gabriel Novak is a 64-year-old retired high-school teacher and a low-risk customer since 1998, with expected activity consisting of pension and Social Security deposits, household spending, and occasional transfers to his own brokerage account.
The account received one inbound wire of $418,500.00 from Bayside Title & Escrow and subsequently transferred $400,000.00 to Novak’s own brokerage account ending 8120.
The inbound wire represented 60.3 times the customer’s expected monthly inflow, causing the large-inflow indicator to fire; no money-mule, structuring, or funnel-account typology matched.
The inbound wire posted on 2026-09-29, and the transfer to the customer’s own brokerage account posted on 2026-10-01.
The review activity occurred from 2026-09-29 through 2026-10-03.
The wire was credited to checking account ending 2954 and the subsequent transfer was sent internally to brokerage account ending 8120.
The customer supplied the settlement statement at the Alameda branch.
The activity was alerted because the $418,500.00 inbound wire was about 60 times the customer’s usual monthly inflow.

The settlement statement identifies the funds as net proceeds from the 2026-09-29 sale of 22 Linden Court, with a sale price of $455,000.00, mortgage payoff of $31,240.00, commissions and fees of $5,260.00, and net proceeds of $418,500.00.
Bayside Title & Escrow, identified as a licensed escrow agent on the settlement statement, disbursed the net sale proceeds by wire to checking account ending 2954.
The customer then transferred $400,000.00 to his own brokerage account, while total posted debits were $400,186.40, or 94.9% of all posted credits.

rationale.text: The unusual inflow is documented by a verified seller settlement statement and is consistent with a home-sale transaction; the funds were transferred to the customer’s own brokerage account rather than a cash-out or unrelated-party channel. No typology matched, and no adverse media or prior alerts were identified.

next_steps: Retain the verified settlement statement and escrow verification in the case record.
Document the no-file decision and the rationale that the activity is consistent with home-sale proceeds.
Monitor for future activity inconsistent with the customer’s stated source of funds or expected activity.
